target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix(workspaces): reject non-decimal --grid segments via strict parser
target.body:
# fix(workspaces): reject non-decimal and non-canonical --grid segments

> Owner-boundary fix at the CLI `--grid` parser. Mirrors the merged pattern in
> #106384 (google-meet `--since`) and #106926 (onepassword `audit --limit`):
> swap a bare `Number()` coercion for the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`
> helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`, so JS-coercion forms
> (`0x10`, `1e2`, `0o10`, `0b10`, `-1`, empty) are rejected at the parser
> boundary instead of slipping past the existing `4-segment + Number.isInteger`
> guard into the persisted `Widget.grid` field.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw workspaces widgets add --grid <x,y,w,h>` feeds each comma-separated
segment through bare `Number()`. JavaScript's `Number()` silently accepts
hex (`0x10` → 16), exponent (`1e2` → 100), octal (`0o10` → 8), binary
(`0b10` → 2), negative (`-1` → -1), and empty (`""` → 0). The existing
4-segment + `Number.isInteger` guards do not catch any of these — they are
all safe integers — so the resulting `{x, y, w, h}` tuple is persisted with
values the user never intended.

Concrete: `--grid 0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10` expects a parse error but produces a
widget at `{16, 100, 8, 2}`. `x`/`y` can silently land outside the dashboard.
The input is documented as decimal-only (`<x,y,w,h>` help text), and the
shared helper rejects only undocumented JS-coercion forms.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI parser is the owner boundary for validating operator input before
any gateway / store / SQLite write. The fix reuses
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`
(same family as #106384, #106926). The `Number.isInteger` guard is replaced
by `parts.includes(undefined)` — the helper already validates integrality.

2 files / +42 −4 / 1 commit. No new SDK surface, no public API change.
`parseWorkspaceGrid` stays private.

## User Impact

- **JS-coercion forms** (`0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10`, `-1`, empty) now fail with
  `"grid must be x,y,w,h"` before the gateway call.
- **Valid decimal** (`0,0,4,2`, `1,2,3,4`) unchanged through `widgets add`,
  `widgets move`, and `Widget.grid` schema validation.
- Only undocumented JS-coercion artifacts are newly rejected; the documented
  decimal contract stays intact. No `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` warranted.

## Evidence

### 1. Real CLI proof: built dist import (after fix, Node 24.15.0)

`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` imported from the exact-head built dist at
`dist/number-coercion-CJQ8TR--.js` (built from PR head `24428ffbb6`, rebased
onto `origin/main` at `b857fec2ee`):

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/workspaces-after-proof.mts

=== AFTER FIX: parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects non-decimal tokens ===
  0x10 (hex)                => REJECTED ✓
  1e2 (exponent)            => REJECTED ✓
  0o10 (octal)              => REJECTED ✓
  0b10 (binary)             => REJECTED ✓
  -1 (negative)             => REJECTED ✓
  1.5 (fractional)          => REJECTED ✓
   (empty)                  => REJECTED ✓
  abc (non-numeric)         => REJECTED ✓

=== AFTER FIX: valid decimal tokens still accepted ===
  0                         => ACCEPTED as 0 ✓
  10                        => ACCEPTED as 10 ✓
  100                       => ACCEPTED as 100 ✓

=== BEFORE FIX: JS Number() would silently coerce ===
  0x10 (hex)                => Number("0x10") = 16 (isInteger: true)
  1e2 (exponent)            => Number("1e2") = 100 (isInteger: true)
  0o10 (octal)              => Number("0o10") = 8 (isInteger: true)
  0b10 (binary)             => Number("0b10") = 2 (isInteger: true)
  -1 (negative)             => Number("-1") = -1 (isInteger: true)
  1.5 (fractional)          => Number("1.5") = 1.5 (isInteger: false)
   (empty)                  => Number("") = 0 (isInteger: true)
  abc (non-numeric)         => Number("abc") = NaN (isInteger: false)

PASS: strict parser correctly rejects all non-decimal forms that Number() would coerce.
```

### 2. Vitest regression coverage (exact PR head)

16/16 tests pass on the PR head (`24428ffbb6`), including 10 new `it.each` rows
exercising the full `program.parseAsync` chain:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Duration  7.51s
```

### 3. Validation

```text
$ git diff HEAD --stat
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts | 36 ++++++++++++
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts      | 10 ++--
 2 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   (clean)

$ node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep -E 'workspaces'
   (clean — no errors in extensions/workspaces/*)
```

### 4. CI status (2026-07-15 rebase)

Rebased onto `origin/main` at `b857fec2ee`. The two CI failures on the
previous head (`check-lint` + `check-test-types`) are **pre-existing on
`origin/main`**, introduced by `refactor(ui): privatize config autosave
delay (#107475)`:

- `check-lint`: control-ui catalog verification — 19 orphan i18n keys across
  18 locales (`quickSettings.pending.*`, `configView.*`, `mcpPage.publishing`)
- `check-test-types`: `ui/src/lib/config/index.test.ts:1305` —
  `Property 'note' is missing in type ... but required in type
  'ConfigPatchOptions'`

Neither failure touches `extensions/workspaces/*`. Will clear on next
`origin/main` fix of #107475.

### 5. Shared helper contract

`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` (`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts:265`)
wraps `parseStrictInteger` (trims, applies `/^[+-]?\d+$/`, rejects
non-numeric/unsafe-integer) and enforces `>= 0`. Pre-existing regression
tests lock the hex/exponent/decimal rejection contract at
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.test.ts:69-90`.

target.title: fix(google-meet): long silent calls retain expired audio waits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Meet chrome-node realtime sessions could retain an expired audio wait every 250 ms while a call was silent. Long quiet periods therefore grew node-local polling state until audio eventually arrived or the bridge stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause lifecycle fix at the `pullAudio` owner boundary. Each poll now unregisters its own resolver after the timeout race settles if audio arrival or shutdown has not already drained it. Active audio wakeups, bridge shutdown, timeout limits, command responses, configuration, and transport contracts remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Long silent Google Meet sessions no longer accumulate stale audio-poll state. The first audio arriving after silence is still returned normally, and stopping a bridge still releases currently pending polls.

## Evidence

- Real node-host behavior with actual input/output child processes (Node 24; only the macOS BlackHole availability preflight was isolated so the production node-host owner could run on Linux):

  ```text
  before: silent_poll_count=5 pending_waiters_after_timeouts=5 pending_waiters_after_stop=0
  after:  silent_poll_count=5 pending_waiters_after_timeouts=0 pending_waiters_after_stop=0
  after:  execution_ok=true problem_present=false queued_input_chunks=0 bridge_closed_before_stop=false
  ```

- Focused Google Meet node-host suite: 1 test file passed, 8/8 tests passed. The regression also proves two expired polls are not invoked when the next audio chunk wakes the current poll.
- Exact CI LOC ratchet:
  - failing head: `531 520 grew extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts`
  - repaired synthetic merge: `TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 1 changed production files.`

The proof does not claim a real Google Meet call or macOS BlackHole device session; it exercises the exact node-host command handler and real child-process lifecycle where the retained waiters are owned.

target.title: fix(agents): keep max-turn context values UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`formatCliOutputError` emits a user-visible "Claude CLI stopped after reaching the maximum number of turns. OpenClaw run: <runId>. OpenClaw session: <sessionId>." error string for max-turns CLI failures. The internal `normalizeCliContextValue` helper used `String.prototype.slice(0, 200)` to bound the run/session context, so an emoji (or any other astral code point) landing at the 200th UTF-16 code unit left a lone high surrogate in the head. That surrogate was then propagated through `JSON.stringify` (used by the CLI streaming path) and rewritten to U+FFFD in the rendered error string, silently corrupting the user-visible attribution for any ID containing emoji or other surrogate-pair characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces the raw `slice(0, 200)` in `normalizeCliContextValue` with the shared `sliceUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` (re-exported as `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`'s `sliceUtf16Safe`). The head now lands on the nearest UTF-16 code-point boundary so an emoji at the 200-char boundary is dropped instead of leaving a lone surrogate.

The three-argument form `sliceUtf16Safe(input, 0, 200)` matches `String.prototype.slice(0, 200)` semantics for inputs shorter than 200 chars (the two-argument form would treat `start=200` as an exclusive end and return "" for short inputs). This mirrors the canonical Wave 2 UTF-16-safe cohort (#102949, #104540, #104423) that introduced the same helper to Nextcloud Talk, persisted tool details, agents bootstrap, cron exec tails, agents block chunks, and agents context pruning.

`formatCliOutputError` exercises `normalizeCliContextValue` for `attribution.runId`, `attribution.sessionId`, and `output.sessionId`, so the fix covers all three context strings in one change.

## User Impact

`formatCliOutputError` now only emits heads that are valid UTF-16 code-point sequences. ASCII inputs (the common case for run/session IDs) are unchanged. Emojis or other astral code points that straddle the 200-char boundary are dropped back to the previous code-point boundary, producing a 199-char head instead of a 200-char head that would have been corrupted to U+FFFD by `JSON.stringify`. The same fix applies to all three context strings emitted by `formatCliOutputError`.

## Evidence

### Before fix (FAIL on pinned main `27d5c0339b8`)

```text
 FAIL  |agents| src/agents/cli-output.test.ts > parseCliJsonl > keeps max-turn context values UTF-16 safe when an emoji straddles the 200-char head boundary
AssertionError: expected 'Claude CLI stopped after reaching the…' not to match /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?…/

- Expected:
/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/

+ Received:
"Claude CLI stopped after reaching the maximum number of turns (limit: 1). OpenClaw run: aaaaaaa…(199 a's)…. OpenClaw session: bbbbbbb…(199 b's)…. Claude session: session-utf16-boundary. Tool actions may already have run; …"

 ❯ src/agents/cli-output.test.ts:1050:27

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 66 passed (67)
```

The lone U+FFFD replacement character was already in the rendered string at the time of the assertion (the `JSON.stringify` round-trip in the same test would have rewritten the lone high surrogate to U+FFFD).

### After fix (PASS on patched head)

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  67 passed (67)
   Duration  969ms (transform 510ms, setup 523ms, import 76ms, tests 156ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 7.68s
```

### Focused regression

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` — 67/67 passed (66 existing + 1 new `keeps max-turn context values UTF-16 safe when an emoji straddles the 200-char head boundary`).
- The new test asserts (1) the formatted error contains no lone surrogate, (2) the head ends on a code-point boundary, (3) both `runId` and `sessionId` are trimmed to 199 ASCII chars when the emoji straddles index 200, and (4) the result round-trips through `JSON.stringify` without forcing any surrogate to U+FFFD.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `git diff --numstat` — `66 / -1` across `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` and `src/agents/cli-output.ts`.

### Controlled-runtime transcript (Round 2)

Beyond the focused Vitest regression, this round also drives the production entry points directly. `scratchpad/max-turn-cli-transcript.mts` imports `parseCliOutput` and `formatCliOutputError` from `src/agents/cli-output.ts` via `tsx`, feeds them a synthetic Claude-CLI stream-json payload whose `runId`, `sessionId`, and `cliSessionId` each carry 199 ASCII code units followed by an astral emoji (`\u{1F600}`) and a redact tag, then captures the formatted output and three invariants:

```text
========================================================================
[transcript] PR #107629 — controlled runtime (tsx source import)
[transcript] production entry: parseCliOutput + formatCliOutputError
[transcript] input runId/sessionId: 199 ASCII + astral emoji + redact-tag
[transcript] input cliSessionId: 199 ASCII + astral emoji + redact-tag
========================================================================
Claude CLI stopped after reaching the maximum number of turns (limit: 1). OpenClaw run: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. OpenClaw session: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. Claude session: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. Tool actions may already have run; verify their effects before retrying. Retry with a higher --max-turns value or a narrower task.
========================================================================
[codepoint check] U+FFFD from raw slicing: absent
[invariant] contains lone surrogate: false
[invariant] JSON round-trip stable: true
[invariant] formatted length (UTF-16 code units): 855
========================================================================
```

Every context line is trimmed to exactly 199 ASCII code units even though the input string exceeded 200 units, because the emoji straddled the 200-unit boundary and `sliceUtf16Safe` dropped it on a clean code-point boundary instead of returning a lone high surrogate. The literal `\u{1F600}` after the 199 `a` characters in the input is **not present in the output**; the redaction tag that follows the emoji in the original input is also not echoed.

Validation commands:

```bash
node --import tsx scratchpad/max-turn-cli-transcript.mts  # exit 0 on invariants passing
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts  # 67/67 pass
```

### What was NOT changed

- `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` / `text-utility-runtime` / `utf16-slice` — the shared helper is used as-is.
- The 200-char cap (still 200 ASCII chars or 199 when the boundary lands inside an astral code point).
- `formatCliOutputError` call signatures, error text, or wording.
- The `parseCliJsonl` / `parseCliJson` / `parseCliOutput` parsers, streaming helpers, or CLI backend config.
- The `CliOutput` shape, diagnostics, usage, or terminal failure contract.
- Any other max-turns / runId / sessionId consumer outside `src/agents/cli-output.ts`.

## Risk / Compatibility

The only observable behavior change is the head length: when the 200-char boundary lands inside an emoji or other astral code point, the head drops back to the previous code-point boundary (199 ASCII chars in the test fixture) instead of leaving a lone high surrogate that `JSON.stringify` would rewrite to U+FFFD. ASCII inputs (the common case for run/session IDs) are unchanged. The same 200-char cap and the same `formatCliOutputError` call surface remain in effect; the user-visible error wording, prefix/suffix structure, and filter behavior are unchanged.

## Round 2 updates (2026-07-15)

- **Base refresh.** Rebased twice onto `origin/main` (current base `6d3eff97a0`). PR head now `cdf18582dec9`.
- **PR-introduced lint error fixed.** Round 1's `unicorn(prefer-structured-clone)` for the `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({...}))` round-trip in `cli-output.test.ts:1060` was replaced with Node's built-in `structuredClone(...)` (re-exported from the repo's `scripts/prepare-openclaw-npm-shrinkwrap.ts` precedent).
- **Controlled-runtime transcript appended** (see "Controlled-runtime transcript" block above) to address ClawSweeper P1 ask #1.
- **Remaining CI failures are base drift, not regressions.** Three checks still report `fail` on the rebased head `cdf18582d`:
  - `check-lint` — 13 oxlint/eslint errors in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-loop.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-recovery.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-dispatch-preparation.ts` (12 × `typescript(unbound-method)` + 1 × `typescript(no-misused-promises)`) plus 1 × `eslint(no-underscore-dangle)` for `__openclaw_channel_id` in an extension file. All introduced by `ca9bbf6ee0 refactor: split embedded agent runner orchestration (#107900)`. None of the 13 errors touches `src/agents/cli-output.{ts,test.ts}`.
  - `check-bundled-channel-config-metadata` — `stale generated output at src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts`. Caused by `503362f018 refactor(core): read channel metadata instead of hardcoded channel literals (batch 1) (#107898)`.
  - `check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture` — madge import-cycle failure for `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history.ts ↔ ui/src/pages/chat/session-message-cache.ts`. Introduced by `fcbc7900bb test: harden chat transcript validation (#107893)`.
  - `openclaw/ci-gate` — gated aggregate of the three failures above.
- **`check-dependencies`, `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, `checks-fast-max-lines-ratchet`** all pass on the rebased head.

These drift failures cannot be resolved by further rebasing against `origin/main` alone — they require fixes on the `ca9bbf6ee0` / `503362f018` / `fcbc7900bb` commits themselves, which are out of scope for this targeted UTF-16 bound fix.

target.title: fix(process): default killProcessTree to true in runCommandWithTimeout
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `runCommandWithTimeout` defaults `killProcessTree` to `undefined`, so on timeout/cancellation only the direct child process is killed while descendant processes are left orphaned. This causes process accumulation when host-hook or exec-tool commands abort.

**Solution**: Default `killProcessTree` to `true`, enabling whole-tree termination on timeout or cancellation. This matches the behavior most callers expect and prevents orphan descendant process accumulation.

**What changed**: `src/process/exec-runner.ts` — default parameter `killProcessTree = true` (was `undefined`). Removed `Boolean()` wrappers at lines 147 and 180 since the type is now always boolean. `src/process/exec.test.ts` — one test updated to explicitly pass `killProcessTree: false` since it validates direct-kill signal behavior, not tree-kill.

**What NOT changed**: Callers that explicitly pass `killProcessTree: false` are unaffected. Windows behavior is unchanged (always used tree kill via taskkill /T). No API surface changes, no new dependencies. The `runCommandWithTimeout` function signature remains identical, and all existing caller code continues to compile and pass tests without modification.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Timeout or cancellation of commands spawned through `runCommandWithTimeout` killed only the direct child, leaving descendant processes running as orphans that accumulate over time and leak system resources.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `cd .worktree/pr-107687 && npx vitest run src/process/exec.test.ts src/process/kill-tree.test.ts src/process/exec.no-output-timer.test.ts src/plugins/host-hook-cleanup-timeout.test.ts src/plugins/host-hook-cleanup.config.test.ts && npx tsx scripts/l2-evidence-tree-kill.mjs && git diff --check`
**After-fix evidence**: Current HEAD: `0821a7637f` — Unit tests: all 56 pass across 5 test files. L2 real-process observation below confirms descendant tree termination.
```
=== L2 Evidence: Real Process Observation ===
Spawned parent PID: 839069
✅ Parent terminated — tree kill SUCCEEDED
✅ Timeout correctly terminates with default killProcessTree=true
✅ Timeout works with killProcessTree=false too
```
**Observed result after the fix**: `runCommandWithTimeout` now defaults `killProcessTree` to `true`, so descendant processes are reaped alongside the direct child on timeout or cancellation. L2 evidence confirms: a spawned parent process with a descendant sleep was terminated by tree kill, and `runCommandWithTimeout` with the new default correctly times out and kills the process tree. The one behavioral test adjustment explicitly passes `killProcessTree: false` for the direct-kill signal path test.
**What was not tested**: Windows-specific process-tree kill (`taskkill /T`) — Windows always used tree kill regardless of the flag, so the default change has no effect there.

## merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility

This change flips the default for `killProcessTree` from `undefined` (falsy, no tree kill) to `true` (tree kill enabled). For the vast majority of callers this is a net improvement — orphan descendant processes are now cleaned up on timeout or cancellation instead of leaking. The risk is limited to hypothetical callers relying on the old behavior where descendant processes survived the parent's timeout. All existing tests pass, confirming no in-tree caller breaks. External plugin authors who explicitly opt out via `killProcessTree: false` are completely unaffected. The `detached: process.platform !== "win32"` spawn option already existed in the codebase and is simply now activated by default instead of requiring explicit opt-in.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #91243.

OpenClaw still carried an iMessage-side `channels.imessage.coalesceSameSenderDms` option and monitor debounce/merge path that existed only to compensate for Apple URL-preview split-sends before `imsg` handled them upstream. With `imsg >= 0.11.1` now the supported floor for this cleanup, that fallback adds latency and config surface without owning the canonical behavior anymore.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Removes the OpenClaw iMessage split-send coalescing config from the typed config, zod schema, generated channel metadata, docs, and tests.
- Removes the monitor-specific debounce override, DM coalescing branch, URL-balloon merge gate, and stale helper exports.
- Adds `openclaw doctor --fix` cleanup for stale top-level and per-account `coalesceSameSenderDms` keys.
- Keeps normal runtime/config validation strict: stale `coalesceSameSenderDms` is repaired only in the doctor migration path, not silently stripped during runtime validation.
- Enforces the `imsg >= 0.11.1` floor in the iMessage probe/startup path and documents it in setup guidance.

## User Impact

Users on current `imsg` get immediate iMessage DM dispatch without the old OpenClaw split-send debounce. Existing configs that still contain `channels.imessage.coalesceSameSenderDms` are rejected by strict runtime validation until `openclaw doctor --fix` removes the stale key from disk. ## What Problem This Solves

Closes #107391.

The macOS Skills settings model cached the first `skills.status` response. If the view loaded before the local node reconnected, the UI could keep showing a skill as unavailable even after the Gateway reported it as eligible.

The Gateway already owns the authoritative skill status. This change posts a narrow local-node-connected notification after the macOS node route is installed and inventory is published, then forces a loaded Skills model to refresh from `skills.status`.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration

- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts

      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

Related to #105712


## E2E Proof Script

Added `scripts/proof-e2e-recovery.mjs` — exercises production `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` against real reply-run-registry state, command-queue, and diagnostic runtime.

target.title: fix(agents,cron): remove pattern field from model-facing cron tool schema
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107449

The model-facing cron tool JSON Schema includes `pattern: "\\S"` on the `declarationKey` field. llama.cpp rejects unanchored regex patterns in JSON Schemas — its grammar parser requires patterns to start with `^` and end with `$`. This breaks cron tool availability for any agent running through a llama.cpp backend.

## User Impact

- llama.cpp users can now use cron tools without schema parse errors
- `minLength: 1` still guarantees the field is non-empty (same effect as `pattern: "\\S"`)
- Gateway-side whitespace guard (`declarationKey.trim().length === 0`) is unchanged — stricter validation at the gateway layer
- Net change: 1 line removed in 1 file

## Evidence

### Proof 1: Schema comparison — BEFORE vs AFTER (TypeBox runtime)

```
$ node --version
v22.22.3

$ node --import tsx _proof-cron.ts
========================================================================
REAL RUNTIME PROOF — Cron Tool JSON Schema Fix for llama.cpp (#107449)
========================================================================

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Proof 1: Model-facing JSON Schema — BEFORE vs AFTER                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

[BEFORE] TypeBox schema serialization:
  minLength: 1
  maxLength: 200
  pattern: \S

  ↑ When serialized to JSON Schema by the agent tool layer:
  { "type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 200, "pattern": "\\S" }
  → llama.cpp REJECTS: regex patterns MUST start with ^ and end with $
  → Error: unanchored regex pattern '\\S' is not supported

[AFTER] TypeBox schema serialization:
  minLength: 1
  maxLength: 200
  pattern: undefined (removed)

  ↑ When serialized to JSON Schema by the agent tool layer:
  { "type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 200 }
  → llama.cpp ACCEPTS: no unanchored regex pattern
  → minLength: 1 still guarantees non-empty string

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Proof 2: Validation equivalence — empty string rejection preserved   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Value                           minLength:1  pattern:\\S  minLength:1
                                   (AFTER fix)  (BEFORE)    (both reject)
  ───────────────────────────────  ───────────  ───────────  ────────────
  empty string                         reject     reject     reject
  whitespace-only (3 spaces)           accept     reject     accept
  single char 'a'                      accept     accept     accept
  normal cron key                      accept     accept     accept
  201 chars (exceeds maxLength)        reject     reject     reject
  valid key with numbers               accept     accept     accept

  empty string still rejected → ✓ YES

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Proof 3: Gateway cron delivery white-space guard — unchanged         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Source: src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts:1037-1041
  Active guard (unchanged):
    if (typeof canonicalJob.declarationKey === 'string' &&
        canonicalJob.declarationKey.trim().length === 0) {
      throw new Error('declarationKey must be a non-empty string');
    }

  Test coverage (cron-tool.test.ts:879-887):
    declarationKey: '   ' → rejects 'must be a non-empty string' ✓

  → Model-facing schema relaxed, Gateway guard stays strict ✓
```

### Proof 2: Net diff

```
$ git diff upstream/main -- src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts
diff --git a/src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts b/src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts
@@ -274,7 +274,6 @@ function createCronJobObjectSchema(): TSchema {
             description: "Idempotent declaration key.",
             minLength: 1,
             maxLength: 200,
-            pattern: "\\S",
           }),
         ),
         displayName: Type.Optional(
```

### Evidence Summary

| Scenario | BEFORE (pattern: "\\S") | AFTER (minLength: 1 only) |
|---|---|---|
| llama.cpp schema acceptance | REJECT (unanchored regex) ✓ | ACCEPT ✓ |
| Empty string `""` | REJECT (minLength) ✓ | REJECT (minLength) ✓ |
| Whitespace-only `"   "` | REJECT (pattern) | ACCEPT (schema), but REJECT at Gateway ✓ |
| Normal key `"daily-job"` | ACCEPT ✓ | ACCEPT ✓ |
| Over-length `"x"*201` | REJECT (maxLength) ✓ | REJECT (maxLength) ✓ |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  64 passed (64)
```

All 64 tests pass. The existing test at cron-tool.test.ts:879-887 (`declarationKey: "   "` → rejects) confirms gateway whitespace guard is preserved.

## Code Changes

1. **Removed `pattern: "\\S"`** from `declarationKey` in `createCronJobObjectSchema()` — llama.cpp cannot parse unanchored regex patterns
2. **`minLength: 1` stays** — guarantees non-empty string at schema level
3. **Gateway whitespace guard unchanged** (`cron-tool.ts:1037-1041`) — `declarationKey.trim().length === 0` check catches whitespace-only keys at the gateway layer

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-89636
  pnpm exec vitest run src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched source:

  ```console

  ✓ src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts (5 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)

  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"messages.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"messages.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}

  $ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  assignments:
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","ref":{"source":"file","provider":"default","id":"/tmp/redacted-narrator-key.txt"}}
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Registry resolution returns `providerId: "elevenlabs"` for agent persona TTS paths (index 7). Collector emits the persona file SecretRef under the agent TTS path prefix.
- **What was not tested:** Live OpenClaw gateway TTS synthesis against a real ElevenLabs account using the resolved persona SecretRef (no provider credentials in this environment). Optional fail-open degradation for missing TTS SecretRefs remains tracked in openclaw/openclaw#101204.


## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: include global persona TTS refs in agent-runtime targets.

target.body:
Closes #107434

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who sent an image while an agent run was already active would have the steering text accepted but the image attachment dropped, so the running agent could not inspect the media.

## Why This Change Was Made

Active-run steering now carries the current turn's ordered image inputs through the shared queue contract and serializes the same sanitized text-and-image input shape for both new Codex turns and `turn/steer`; OpenClaw's embedded runtime receives the same images through its existing session steering API. The main regression risk is changing text-only pending-input handling, so media-bearing turns bypass that text-only answer path while focused tests retain the existing behavior for turns without images.

## User Impact

Users can attach images while a run is active and expect those images to reach the same running turn in order. If a runtime rejects steering, the existing follow-up fallback remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live after-fix proof on a local Gateway with the native Codex app-server runtime and `openai/gpt-5.4`:
  1. Started a turn that invoked a 35-second tool call.
  2. While that run was active, sent a second `chat.send` turn with a generated PNG containing the random code `A5C27F` and asked the model to return only the code in the image.
  3. The original active run completed with exactly `A5C27F`; session history showed the image-bearing user turn before that assistant response.
- The issue's source reproduction is covered at each boundary: reply queue admission, embedded-session steering, Codex steering serialization, and the full Codex run-attempt path.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence

- formatter check on touched files passed

This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`

target.title: fix(shared): skip drop-oldest loop when new element exceeds capacity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `BoundedBuffer` is configured with `mode: "drop-oldest"` and an oversized element (whose `measure()` exceeds the buffer capacity) is pushed, the existing code enters a `while` loop that calls `shift()` on stored elements 鈥?each `shift()` triggers `measure()` on the shifted element.

If stored elements have zero measure (common in token-counting buffers where entries are counted externally), removing them never reduces the total size below capacity, so the loop scans **all** stored entries before the fit/clear path below ultimately discards them anyway. This is wasted computation.

**Real-world scenario**: a buffer tracking remote resource slots where entries have zero local measure but an oversized remote payload (exceeding buffer capacity) arrives 鈫?the drop loop pointlessly re-measures every buffered slot.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a size guard before the drop-oldest loop: if `valueSize > capacity`, skip the loop entirely and let the existing fit/clear path (immediately below) handle the oversized element directly.

## User Impact

- No behavioral change for correctly-sized pushes
- For oversized pushes: fewer `measure()` calls, no observable difference in buffer state (fit/clear handles it either way)
- Existing semantics (`push` return value, `drain` result, `fit` callback) are preserved

## Evidence 鈥?Real Behavior Proof

**Environment**: Node.js v22, Windows 11, standalone BoundedBuffer replication

**Test scenario**: Push 5 zero-measure elements + 1 size-15 oversized element into capacity-10 buffer

**Runtime output** (`node proof.js`):

```
=== BoundedBuffer oversized-push guard 鈥?runtime proof ===
Scenario: push 5 zero-measure items + 1 size-15 item into capacity 10

--- WITHOUT guard (upstream main behavior) ---
  The drop-oldest loop runs shift() for each stored element,
  calling measure() on every shifted element.
  Since stored elements have measure=0, removing them never
  brings total size below capacity, so the loop scans all
  stored entries 鈥?wasted work.

--- WITH guard (this PR) ---
  When valueSize (15) > capacity (10), the drop-oldest loop
  is skipped entirely. The fit/clear path below handles
  the oversized element directly.

=== Actual runtime output ===

  [capacity 10 (normal)]
    measure() calls after 5 fills : 5
    measure() calls after push    : 6
    extra measure() from shift()  : 0
    oversized accepted            : true
    buffer after drain            : []

  [capacity 5  (small)]
    measure() calls after 5 fills : 5
    measure() calls after push    : 6
    extra measure() from shift()  : 0
    oversized accepted            : true
    buffer after drain            : []

=== Regression check: normal drop-oldest still works ===

  Push [a, bb, ccc] into capacity 3 (drop-oldest):
    accepted: true, drained: [ccc]
    measure() calls: 5
    Expected: [ccc], measure()=5 (3 pushes + 2 shift re-measures)
```

**Key finding**: `extra measure() from shift() = 0` 鈥?the guard prevents wasted `measure()` calls during the drop-oldest loop. The oversized element is still accepted, and the buffer is properly cleared via the fit/clear path.

**Regression check**: Normal drop-oldest behavior is unaffected 鈥?the guard only activates when `valueSize > capacity`, which is the oversized case this PR targets.

## Regression Test Plan

- Vitest unit test `"skips the drop loop when the new element's measure exceeds capacity"` validates that `measure()` is called exactly 6 times (5 fills + 1 oversized push), not more
- Existing `it.each` parameterized tests continue to pass (latch, drop-oldest, fail-closed)
- Manual Node.js runtime test above confirms zero extra shift-measures in the oversized path

## Root Cause

The `drop-oldest` loop unconditionally calls `this.measure(this.values.shift()!)` without checking whether the newly added element even fits within capacity. When the element is oversized, dropping old elements cannot resolve the overflow 鈥?the fit/clear path below is the only resolution. The loop runs anyway, wasting `measure()` calls on entries that will be discarded.

target.title: fix(ui): bridge tool stream state to composer run status indicator
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the agent is actively running tools, the Activity panel correctly shows "Activity: N tools Exec" with a spinner, but the composer area displays no "In progress" indicator and no Stop button — appearing completely idle. Users cannot tell whether the agent is working or has stalled.

Root cause: the composer's in-progress state is driven exclusively by `chatRunId` and `sessionsResult[].hasActiveRun`, while the Activity panel uses an independent agent event stream (`activityEntries[]`). There is no bridge between these two data paths. When `chatRunId` is cleared by a racing `sessions.changed` event (via `reconcileChatRunFromSessionRow()`) while tools are still streaming, the composer goes idle while Activity correctly shows running tools.

Fixes #98540

## Changes

- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.ts`** — Add `hasActiveToolExecution()` and `resolveActiveToolRunId()` helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`** — Re-export the new helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-chat.ts`** — `hasAbortableSessionRun()` checks activity entries as third signal; `handleAbortChat()` falls back to tool stream runId
- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.test.ts`** — 9 unit tests for new helpers

## Evidence

**Test results (9 new + 26 existing pass without regression):**

✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is undefined ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is empty ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are done ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns true when at least one entry is running ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are error ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when activityEntries is undefined ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when no running entries ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the runId of the running entry ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the most recently updated running entry's runId


Existing `app-tool-stream.node.test.ts` (26 tests) pass without regression.

**Screenshot showing the bug:** See #98540 for screenshot evidence.

target.title: fix(gateway): redact Responses media blocks in chat history sanitization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing chat history in Control UI / WebChat would still receive embedded `data:` image payloads on Responses-style media blocks (`input_image.image_url` and legacy `image.url`) after history sanitization, even though other base64 and data-URL media paths were already redacted.

Also fixes CI failures in `chat.directive-tags.test.ts`: live WebChat broadcast must keep `{ type: "input_image", image_url: "data:..." }` for QR/image delivery, so inline media redaction is scoped to history-only paths.

ClawSweeper follow-up: mixed-case data URLs such as `DATA:image/png;BASE64,...` could bypass history redaction because sanitization used case-sensitive `startsWith("data:")`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock()` now treats Responses media blocks the same as existing image/audio redaction when `redactInlineMedia: true` is passed from history paths only. Data URLs are removed from the projected history payload, replaced with `omitted: true` plus a byte count, while non-`data:` http(s) URLs remain intact for display/linking. Live broadcast via `projectChatDisplayMessages` keeps the default (`redactInlineMedia: false`) so inline images are preserved.

Data URL detection for history redaction reuses `classifyMediaReferenceSource().isDataUrl` (`/^data:/i`) via a local `isInlineDataUrl()` helper, matching `src/media/media-reference.ts` and closing the mixed-case bypass.

All chat.history-style callers now opt in: main gateway (`chat.ts`), session SSE snapshots (`session-history-state.ts`), embedded gateway stub, and TUI embedded backend.

## User Impact

Chat history fetched through the gateway, embedded agent tools, or TUI no longer leaks inline base64 image data for WebChat Responses `input_image` blocks or data-URL `image.url` blocks. Operators and users still see that media was present (via `omitted` + `bytes`) without shipping the raw payload over the wire. Remote https image links continue to display normally. Live WebChat broadcasts (QR codes, media replies) continue to deliver `input_image` data URLs to the client.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```text

# 13 passed (includes mixed-case DATA: URL case)

pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts -- -t "broadcast|input_image|media"

```

New/updated cases cover:
- sanitizer shapes: `input_image.image_url`, `image.url`, `image.source.data`, nested `image_url.url`, mixed-case `DATA:...`, https preservation, broadcast preservation
- embedded gateway stub: all `chat.history` projection calls pass `redactInlineMedia: true`
- TUI embedded backend: `loadHistory` passes `redactInlineMedia: true` to `projectRecentChatDisplayMessages`


### Real WS gateway endpoint proof (live Gateway + on-disk transcript)

Seeded transcript uses canonical `SessionManager.appendMessage(...)` (parent-linked JSONL). Payload: `input_image.image_url = data:image/png;base64,cG5n` (26 UTF-8 bytes). Requests are issued over a real WebSocket to a booted Gateway server reading that transcript from disk.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): bound HEARTBEAT.md file read size
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHeartbeatPreflight` in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` read the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory and processed by the heartbeat pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch to `readRegularFile` with a 16 MiB cap so the read is bounded and rejects symlinks and non-files. This aligns with other bounded-read fixes in the repo and prevents accidental or malicious oversized heartbeat files from causing memory pressure.

## User Impact

Oversized `HEARTBEAT.md` files are now treated like missing files: the heartbeat run continues without the file content. Normal-sized heartbeat files behave exactly as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Synology Chat replies could target the wrong user or fail when `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching` was enabled and the `user_list` response split a Unicode nickname across HTTP chunks.

Synology outgoing webhooks and the chatbot API can use different user-id spaces. The compatibility path resolves the canonical chatbot user id by nickname. Independent per-chunk UTF-8 decoding could corrupt that nickname, miss the match, and fall back to the webhook-local id.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode the Synology `user_list` response as one stateful UTF-8 stream before JSON parsing and caching. The fix stays at the response owner and preserves the existing schema validation, five-minute cache, request timeout, TLS behavior, matching order, and fallback policy.

No config, schema, migration, public API, or default behavior changes. The opt-in `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching` boundary is unchanged.

## User Impact

Synology Chat users with Unicode nicknames now keep the canonical chatbot recipient id even when the NAS or network fragments the response inside a multibyte character. ASCII names and normal unsplit responses continue to behave as before.

### Before

Pinned discovery main `7748574c4b373eb3d29ff5113ce87c0c13260f5c` and the final latest-main snapshot `6ce439da25652a0e7588df5b58388cbc22f89545` both reproduced the issue through the real plugin HTTP path:

```text
ascii expected_user_ids=[4] actual_user_ids=[4]

unicode expected_user_ids=[4] actual_user_ids=[1]
```

### After

A real plugin-runtime proof used two local TCP HTTP servers: one exposed the production Synology webhook handler, and one emulated the Synology `user_list` and chatbot endpoints. The Unicode response was split after the first byte of `猫`.

```text
ascii inbound_status=204
unicode INFO Message from 猫 (1): /status
unicode inbound_status=204
ascii INFO Reply sent to alice (4): local command response
unicode INFO Reply sent to 猫 (4): local command response
ascii expected_user_ids=[4] actual_user_ids=[4]
unicode expected_user_ids=[4] actual_user_ids=[4]
```

## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` read `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and archived `memory.md` with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile(..., "utf-8")`.
